name: read_presentation_context
description: Read the current presentation file, slide inventory, selection and template context in one call. Returns title, slide_count, slide_width_points / slide_height_points, is_default_theme, has_content, theme_palette, theme_fonts, template_body_font_pt, content_language, display_language, masters (layouts with ids), slides_metadata (1-based position to stable slide id), the selection and a structure_fingerprint. Optional template or selection failures do not discard the file inventory. The fingerprint tracks slide and shape IDs, not the title, text or styling.

name: list_slide_shapes
description: List all shapes on a slide with their refs, names, types, positions and text (each shape's text cut at 400 characters). Call this before read_slide_text or edit_slide_text — those tools accept only the `ref` field from this output. Refs encode both slide and shape so they cannot be mismatched.

slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or verify_slides output.

name: edit_slide_chart
description: Edit an existing chart, or build a chart form create_slide_chart refuses (combo, 3D, pie, secondary axis), by manipulating raw OOXML; also for surgical XML edits to a chart. For NEW charts of a standard form, prefer create_slide_chart. Never approximate charts with geometric shapes.

slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or verify_slides output.

code.description: Body of an async function with zip (a JSZip archive) and markDirty already in scope: write the statements directly; do not wrap them in a function such as async ({ zip, markDirty }) => { ... }, which is defined but never called, so nothing is written. The exported slide is always ppt/slides/slide1.xml regardless of slide id. The package holds only this slide: media, charts and layouts of other slides are not reachable. After a package replacement the slide id changes; follow the returned id mapping and call list_slide_shapes again before further edits. Read a part with await zip.file(path).async("string"), write it with zip.file(path, xml), and call markDirty() or the edit is discarded; code may also only read and return data. escapeXml(text) escapes text embedded in XML; a bare & silently drops every following run. buildChart(spec) returns template chart XML and insertChart(zip, spec) performs a full templated insert.

autosize_shape_ids.description: cNvPr IDs of shapes whose text body you modified. For shapes already at AutoSizeShapeToFitText, the tool re-applies that setting after reimport so the layout engine recalculates dimensions for verify_slides; shapes at any other autoSize mode are left unchanged. For tables, the tool re-writes each row.height to its current value to trigger frame re-layout (font-only edits don't reflow the rendered table frame on their own). Omit if you only changed non-text content (positions, fills, images).

name: create_slide_chart
description:
Create a chart on a slide from a declarative spec — the default way to add a new chart. Code builds the chart XML from templates that encode the house chart standard (no legends, deleted value axes on bar forms, accent-based emphasis, units carried in number formats), so this is faster and more reliable than writing chart OOXML by hand. Supports column, horizontal bar, line, slope, stacked column with totals, 100% stacked (Likert) bar, waterfall, scatter, and big-number forms. The inserted chart is ordinary chart XML — editable afterwards with edit_built_chart using a full spec, or edit_slide_chart for surgical XML edits. For chart forms outside this list, or fine-grained changes, use edit_slide_chart.

- Send the form, the categories, the raw numbers, a number format that always carries the full unit (on stacked forms the totals format carries the unit and segments are bare), the index of the one category or point that is the message, and a style.
- Always pass a style: the accent from theme_palette on a templated deck or the accent you set in the master on a blank one, the deck body font, and its neutrals.
- Under a deck standard, call read_chart_style on a slide with one of the deck's charts first and pass its settings as style and construction; pass a title when the deck's charts carry a native one. Never guess a font or colour.
- On a line, pass series[].point_labels chosen for the story and the space; for forecast periods pass forecast_from. Pass growth_arrows for straight bar-to-bar arrows; draw elbow arrows or difference markers with edit_slide_xml.

slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or verify_slides output.

spec.description: Declarative chart spec: pick the chart form, supply raw numbers and display formats, and the builder emits known-good chart XML following the house construction standard. No OOXML knowledge needed. Fields under properties apply to every form that lists them.

position.description: Chart frame placement in EMU; omit for the full-slide default

style.description: Colors and font the chart uses. Pass the deck's own accent and fonts so charts follow the deck; omitted values fall back to the house palette (blue accent, grays, Calibri), which is only right on the stock theme

accent.description: The one emphasis color; the deck's accent (theme_palette.accent1, or the accent set in the master)

negative.description: Waterfall decreases; defaults to a warm orange

neutral.description: Non-accent bars and lines; defaults to a mid gray

totals.description: Waterfall totals and totals labels; defaults to dark gray

text.description: Label and axis text; defaults to near-black

text_secondary.description: Axis titles, subtitles; defaults to dark gray

bg.description: The slide background behind the chart. Growth-arrow labels and forecast hatching fill against this, so pass it on any deck whose background is not white

ramp.description: Dark-to-light neutral ramp for Likert and stacked segments

font.description: Typeface for every text in the chart; the deck's body font

construction.description: How the chart is constructed. Omit for the house standard. Under a deck standard, read one of the deck's existing charts and set these to match it (legend position, value axis shown or hidden, gridlines); a title inside the chart is the top-level `title`

value_axis.description: House default hidden on bar forms; line and scatter keep theirs

gridlines.description: Horizontal value gridlines; house default off

point_labels.description: Custom label text for specific points, e.g. [{index: 0, text: '16.3 万辆'}]. index is against categories/values in the caller's display order (same convention as categories), regardless of the builder's internal bottom-up storage order for a horizontal bar chart. Overrides the auto value label (number_format) only for the listed points; other points keep the default value label.

title.description: Optional native chart title. House default is NO native title (omit this; nothing renders in the title area) — use it only when a chart genuinely needs its own headline

subtitle.description: The chart's descriptive label, as a second line under title, worded as the charts skill says

values.description: Bars grow from zero, so values are non-negative; a mixed-sign comparison belongs on a different form

accent_index.description: Index of the one category that is the message; all others render neutral gray

number_format.description: OOXML formatCode. Always include the full unit (prefix and suffix) so every data label reads with it: '"$"#,##0"M"' → $42M, '0"%"' → 38%, '#,##0" people"' → 1,240 people. A bare "#,##0" leaves the reader guessing the unit

forecast_from.description: First forecast category index (0-based). From this point on, bars are hatched (diagonal pattern in the same colors) so they read as projected, not actual. Also append 'E' to those categories' labels

label.description: The change, with sign and unit, e.g. '+21%'

from.description: Category index the arrow starts on; defaults to the arrow's own index

to.description: Category index the arrow ends on; defaults to from + 1

growth_arrows.description: A straight-line arrow drawn over the chart from one bar top to another with the change number centered on the line (opaque slide-background fill so it sits on the arrow). One entry per arrow: {from: 0, to: 1, label: '+21%'} for an adjacent pair, {from: 0, to: N-1, label: '+38%'} for a first-to-last total. Draw arrows only where the change is significant

name: read_chart_style
description: Read every native chart on a slide and return its style as the fields create_slide_chart's spec takes: form (the spec's type: column/bar/line/…), fonts (or font_inherits_theme), explicit fill hexes and scheme colors, legend position, value axis shown or hidden, gridlines, native title, data-label position, gap width, and anything the builder cannot reproduce (combo, 3D, pie, secondary axis). Use this before create_slide_chart under a deck standard, instead of reading raw XML: pass what it returns as style and construction so the new chart matches the deck.

slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or verify_slides output.

name: edit_slide_master
description: Edit slide master and layouts via OOXML — set backgrounds, decorative elements (accent lines, dividers, borders), branding shapes, fonts, theme colors, and placeholders. Use this for any visual element that should appear on all slides, and for theme, rebrand and deck-wide layout work. The modified package is imported with a unique theme identity and slides are mapped to the new layouts by exact name; the result reports ambiguous or missing mappings, and whether the old master could not be deleted.

code.description: Body of an async function with zip (a JSZip archive) and markDirty already in scope: write the statements directly; do not wrap them in a function such as async ({ zip, markDirty }) => { ... }, which is defined but never called, so nothing is written. The package holds the exported first slide and its structure; master and theme parts are ppt/slideMasters/slideMaster1.xml, ppt/slideLayouts/slideLayoutN.xml and ppt/theme/theme1.xml. Read a part with await zip.file(path).async("string"), write it with zip.file(path, xml), and call markDirty() or the edit is discarded; code may also only read and return data. escapeXml(text) escapes text embedded in XML; a bare & silently drops every following run.

name: read_slide_text
description:
Read the raw OOXML paragraph XML (the <a:p> elements, DrawingML a: prefix) from a shape's text body, to inspect existing text content, formatting, bullets, and styles before editing. Change existing text with edit_slide_text, edit_slide_xml or find_and_replace; presentation_apply_patch update_shape with text resets run formatting, so use it only for text you composed.

Key elements:
- <a:p> paragraph, <a:r> text run, <a:t> text content
- <a:pPr> paragraph properties: algn="l|ctr|r|just", lvl (0-based indent level), marL/indent, <a:lnSpc>/<a:spcBef>/<a:spcAft> with <a:spcPts val="1400"/> (hundredths of a pt)
- bullets inside <a:pPr>: <a:buChar char="•"/>, <a:buAutoNum type="arabicPeriod"/>, <a:buNone/>, <a:buFont typeface="Arial"/>
- <a:rPr> run properties: sz (hundredths of a pt, sz="1600" = 16 pt), b="1", i="1", u="sng", lang, baseline; <a:hlinkClick r:id="rId2"/> is a hyperlink
- colour: <a:solidFill><a:schemeClr val="tx2"/></a:solidFill> (theme) or <a:solidFill><a:srgbClr val="FF0000"/></a:solidFill> (explicit)
- <a:latin typeface="Calibri"/> an explicit font

ref.description: Shape reference from list_slide_shapes output (e.g., "258:5"). Encodes both the slide and the shape — do not construct manually, only pass back refs you were given.

name: read_slide_image
description: Render one PowerPoint slide as a PNG for visual inspection. Use slide IDs returned by read_presentation_context.

width.description: PNG width in pixels. Defaults to 960.

height.description: PNG height in pixels. Defaults to 540 on a 16:9 slide (the slide's aspect ratio at the width).

name: edit_slide_text
description:
Replace the paragraph content of a shape with raw OOXML <a:p> XML. The tool preserves the shape's <a:bodyPr> and <a:lstStyle>, but NOT per-run formatting — that lives on each <a:r>'s own <a:rPr>, inside the paragraphs you are replacing. If the shape's <a:lstStyle> is empty (common), a new run with no <a:rPr> falls back to the layout/master default, not the old run's color/size/font. Call read_slide_text first.

Rules for paragraph XML you write (here or with edit_slide_xml):
- OOXML is fully explicit: copy <a:pPr> and <a:rPr> verbatim from the read and change only what was asked; an omitted b="1" means the text is no longer bold.
- Keep <a:schemeClr>; replacing it with hex detaches text from the theme.
- Do not add <a:latin> unless the user asked for a font; text inherits the theme fonts.
- Set lang on <a:rPr> to the text's language (zh-CN for Chinese, en-US for English) or omit it; never force en-US.
- Bullets are <a:buChar> in <a:pPr>, never a "•" in the text. Top-level bullets are lvl="0" or no lvl; sub-bullets lvl="1". A header is level 0 with <a:buNone/>, not a level.
- Bullet indent: inside a body placeholder do not set marL or indent; the paragraph inherits the master. In a text box you added, use the deck master's level-1 values; only when they are unknown use marL="228600" indent="-228600". When extending a list, copy its values.
- Footnote marks are <a:rPr baseline="30000"/>.
- Title alignment follows the layout: centred on Title Slide and Section Header, left on content layouts. A template's own placeholder alignment wins.

Top-level bullet paragraph (do NOT use <a:buNone/> or lvl="1" for regular bullets):
<a:p><a:pPr><a:buFont typeface="Arial"/><a:buChar char="•"/></a:pPr><a:r><a:rPr sz="1600"/><a:t>Bullet text</a:t></a:r></a:p>

Header paragraph (no bullet):
<a:p><a:pPr><a:buNone/></a:pPr><a:r><a:rPr sz="1600" b="1"/><a:t>Header text</a:t></a:r></a:p>

ref.description: Shape reference from list_slide_shapes output (e.g., "258:5"). Encodes both the slide and the shape — do not construct manually, only pass back refs you were given.

code.description: Raw OOXML <a:p> paragraph XML to replace the shape's text content

name: edit_slide_xml
description:
Edit raw OOXML of a PowerPoint slide for what the other slide tools cannot express: existing table cell text, precise run formatting, grouping, custom XML manipulation. Two or more text edits on one slide go in one call.

- Coordinates are EMU (12700 per point).
- Preserve <a:bodyPr> and <a:lstStyle> when replacing a <p:txBody>; paragraph XML follows the rules in edit_slide_text.
- Table cell text lives in <a:tbl>/<a:tr>/<a:tc>. Table height derives from rows and content; <a:ext cy> writes are ignored, so shorten copy or reduce cell fonts and pass the table id in autosize_shape_ids.
- Recolouring an existing SVG icon means editing the SVG in ppt/media/ through its <asvg:svgBlip r:embed> relationship; setting the shape fill colours the box behind it.

name: verify_slides
description: Verify slides for overlapping-shape candidates, out-of-bounds positioning, and low-contrast text. Returns structured results per slide with a `slideId` field, plus `total_slides` / `from_slide` / `to_slide` coverage metadata. When a shape's font color fails WCAG AA (4.5:1) against its own solid fill, a `contrast_warnings` array lists `{shape_id, shape_name, font_color, bg_color, ratio, msg}` — inspect and fix genuine defects before declaring the slide done. To read or edit a flagged shape's text, call list_slide_shapes with that slideId to get refs. For large decks, call with a slide range (0-based indexes, one less than the 1-based slides_metadata position: `{from_slide: 0, to_slide: 19}` is slides 1 to 20) to avoid truncation; if `to_slide < total_slides - 1`, call again for the remainder. Geometry overlap remains a candidate until visually confirmed because intentional layering can produce false positives.

from_slide.description: 0-based index of the first slide (the slides_metadata position minus 1). Defaults to 0 (first slide).

to_slide.description: 0-based index of the last slide, inclusive (the slides_metadata position minus 1). Defaults to from_slide + 19 (a page of 20 slides); the result's to_slide says where it stopped.

name: verify_slide_visual
description: Independent visual review of one slide. Captures a fresh render of the slide and its measured geometry; a separate reviewer that sees nothing of this conversation checks them against an objective defect list (overlaps, overflow, collisions, accidental sibling inconsistency, off-centre badge numbers, unreadable text, low contrast, detached connectors, leftover placeholders). List what you changed in expected_changes so the review also confirms each change or reports it NOT VISIBLE. Returns verdict done or needs_work with the defects to repair, and the render it reviewed.

slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or a patch result.

expected_changes.description: One line per change you made on this slide.

name: find_and_replace
description:
Find and replace text across the whole deck in ONE call — use this for any bulk text replacement (renames, rebrands, term changes) instead of editing shapes one at a time with edit_slide_text/edit_slide_xml. Searches every text run in all shapes (grouped shapes and placeholders included), tables, and speaker notes, at the OOXML level.

Formatting is preserved: a match inside one run keeps that run's formatting; a match that spans runs (e.g. a word split by a mid-word formatting change or spellcheck artifact) is replaced with the first run's formatting. Returns a structured report: total and per-pair replacement counts, per-slide locations (shape, table cell, notes), and anything skipped with a reason. Never edited (matches reported as skipped instead): auto-generated fields, chart and SmartArt text, and slide-layout/master text (use edit_slide_master for those). Matches spanning a line break are skip-reported, not replaced. Run with dry_run:true first when you want to preview match counts before editing.

find.description: Text to find. Plain text, not a regex.

replace.description: Replacement text in its base casing (see preserve_case). May be empty to delete the text.

pairs.description: Find/replace pairs, applied in order — each pair runs over the text the previous pair produced.

match.description: Default "whole_word": matches only where the term is not adjacent to an ASCII letter or digit, so replacing "form" leaves "information" untouched. "substring" also replaces inside longer words.

case_sensitive.description: Default false: occurrences are found regardless of casing.

preserve_case.description: Default false (every match becomes the literal replacement). When true, each occurrence keeps its casing style: ALL-CAPS stays ALL-CAPS, Capitalized stays Capitalized, lowercase stays lowercase — replacing Atlasware→Novagrid turns ATLASWARE into NOVAGRID and atlasware into novagrid.

slide_ids.description: Limit the operation to these slides. Omit entirely to process every slide in the deck (an empty list is rejected rather than widened to the whole deck).

include_notes.description: Default true: speaker notes are searched and replaced along with slide text.

dry_run.description: Default false. When true, reports match counts and locations per slide without changing anything.

name: presentation_apply_patch
description:
Compose or revise 1-3 slides as typed native PowerPoint objects (the default way to build a page). Give each page a slide_ref and an ordered list of operations in PowerPoint points; the executor enforces the design rules that hand-written scripts get wrong: text roles carry font presets and minimum sizes (body >= 14 pt), colors/fonts resolve from design_system tokens so every page shares one palette, and text on a shape goes into the shape's own frame so badges and labels are centred. Pass the latest structure_fingerprint (from read_presentation_context or the previous patch's structure_fingerprint_after); a stale fingerprint is rejected before any mutation. This tool never produces HTML or an intermediate PPTX.

1. Design system first. On the first patch of a new or restyled deck, declare design_system once: colour tokens (add accent2, line, code_bg as needed) and fonts.heading / fonts.body. On a templated deck take them from theme_palette and theme_fonts; for a requested rebrand derive them from the supplied reference. Register the whole background, card, text and accent relationship; never keep an old background palette and swap in new accents. Later patches reference colours by token so pages cannot drift; a palette change is one coherent new design_system, not per-shape hex edits.
2. Roles, not sizes. Give every text a role: title, subtitle, section (small eyebrow label), body, label, caption, footnote, badge (a number or short word centred in a shape), number (a hero figure) or code. Roles carry size, weight, alignment and margins and have accessibility floors; a font_size under a role's floor is rejected, so trim copy or enlarge the container instead. Choose sizes from the slide-design hierarchy; for a template body size under the body floor, omit the role and set text_style.font_size.
3. Text on a shape goes in the shape. Badges, step numbers, chips and labelled boxes are one add_shape with text and role "badge" or "label". Never stack an add_text on a shape to fake centring.
4. Repeat with identical values. Siblings use the same width, height, role, fill token and spacing, computed from one grid (for example three 252 pt columns with 34 pt gutters starting at 48 pt) and reused verbatim wherever the pattern repeats.
5. Layouts and placeholders. Prefer a real layout_id over Blank, and rotate layouts across the deck. On a freshly created slide set clear_existing_shapes: true only when your composition replaces every placeholder, never on a page with user content. Fill or delete every placeholder on a slide you just added; empty placeholders still render. Delete placeholders only on slides you added: on an existing slide a placeholder with text is the user's content. A direct user request to remove a specific placeholder is still honoured. Measure the title band before placing content under it: list_slide_shapes on the new slide, then read the title placeholder's top + height; title bands vary between templates. To move an existing slide onto another layout, give its slide_id with the new layout_id.
6. One slide per patch while building. Each result returns slides[].slide_id, every created shape's shape_id and ref, and structure_fingerprint_after; pass that fingerprint as the next patch's base_structure_fingerprint instead of re-reading. Fix a page with update_shape / delete_shape on the returned ids, not by rebuilding it. Several slides in one patch are fine for slide deletes, reorders or one identical change across slides. Delete or reorder with {"slide_ref": "S4", "slide_id": <id>, "delete_slide": true} or {"slide_ref": "S2", "slide_id": <id>, "move_to": 1}; slide-level changes run after the content edits in the patch.
7. Images and charts. Publish an image with publish_office_asset, list its descriptor under assets with a short key, and place it with add_image. Charts are not operations here: leave their space in the patch and create them with create_slide_chart.
8. Canvas. Every operation stays inside the slide size. Set explicit left and top on every shape.
9. Containers fit their content. Size a card or bar to its text plus 16 to 24 pt of padding; text sitting on a shape is inset 10 to 15 pt from its edges. Fill the page with content, larger type within the hierarchy or wider gutters, never by stretching empty containers. Stacked layers share one left edge unless the stagger carries meaning.
10. Stacking. Operations stack in the order listed; list background shapes first, and fix an existing shape's stacking with update_shape z_order.
11. Connectors and diagrams. Diagram slides (process flows, timelines, cycles, org charts) are built here: add_shape nodes with label or badge text, add_connector with end_arrow between them, all on one grid. For every node-to-node link set start_anchor and end_anchor and pick the edge (left, right, top, bottom); normally omit offset for the midpoint (use 0.15 to 0.85 only to separate parallel ports; never a rounded corner). Straight is a direct relation; Elbow is a simple orthogonal one. A feedback loop or a route that must avoid objects is one logical Straight connector with waypoints. Never fake one route with several arrowed connectors, separate triangles or hairline rectangles. Raw left/top/width/height is only for a free-floating line. To repair a connector, delete_shape it and add an anchored one in the same patch; after moving a node, recreate its routes.
12. Tables. add_table already applies the slide-table style; mark the message with highlight_rows or highlight_columns, and use table_style "host_default" only when matching a deck whose tables use PowerPoint's built-in style. Size before inserting: a single-line row is about 30 pt, a two-line row about 50 pt; compute what fits and split rather than run off the slide. Cells over about 40 words belong in a text box or footnote instead. Restyle an existing table with update_table.

design_system.description: Design tokens declared once for the deck and remembered for later patches in this session. Colors are referenced by token name anywhere a color is accepted; fonts by heading/body/mono. Declare at least accent, text, muted, bg and card.

slide_ref.description: Your stable label for this page (e.g. S3). Echoed in the result.

slide_id.description: Current slide id to edit an existing page. Omit to create a new slide.

layout_id.description: A layout id from read_presentation_context.masters (prefer a real layout over Blank). On a new slide it picks the layout; with slide_id it re-applies that layout to the existing slide (alone, or before this slide's operations). Then call list_slide_shapes: the slide's placeholders follow the new layout.

slide_master_id.description: The master that owns layout_id; needed only when the same layout id exists under more than one master.

position.description: New slides only: 1-based position, counted before this patch deletes any slide. Use move_to for an existing slide.

background.description: 6-digit hex color (with or without #) or a design_system color token such as "accent".

clear_existing_shapes.description: New slides only: delete the layout placeholders the new slide inherited before applying operations. Rejected when slide_id targets an existing page; use delete_shape for specific shapes there.

delete_slide.description: Existing slides only (slide_id required): delete the whole slide. Give no operations, background, layout_id or move_to with it. Runs after every other change in the patch; the deck must keep at least one slide.

move_to.description: Existing slides only (slide_id required): final 1-based position of this slide. May be combined with operations on the same slide, or used alone (omit operations) for a pure reorder, which needs no new visual review.

items.description: One native operation. add_text: a text box (role + text). add_shape: a geometric shape; when it carries text the text lives in the shape's own frame and is centred (use role "badge" for numbers/short labels). add_connector: a deterministic native OOXML connector or routed sequence of connector segments, optionally with one native terminal arrowhead. For node-to-node diagrams use start_anchor/end_anchor so the executor resolves visible edge points; use raw left/top/width/height only for free-floating lines. add_image: an image-filled rectangle from assets[].key. add_table: a native table from string values, styled as a slide table by default (bold header without fill, rules between rows only, bold first column, numeric columns right-aligned). update_table: restyle an existing native table by shape_id (cell ranges, row rules, row height, column widths). update_shape / delete_shape: existing shape ids from list_slide_shapes or a previous patch result.

name.description: Stable readable shape name, e.g. card2-title. Reported back with the created shape id.

text.description: Required for add_text; optional on add_shape (rendered inside the shape) and update_shape (replaces the text; run formatting is reset). Use \n for a line/paragraph break inside multi-line text (e.g. an analysis card's bullet lines) — it is rendered as a real PowerPoint paragraph break, not a literal backslash-n.

role.description: Typography preset. Sizes/floors in pt: title 32/28, subtitle 18/16, section 12/11, body 16/14, label 14/12, caption 12/11, footnote 10/9, badge 16/12 (centred, no wrap, zero margins), number 28/20, code 14/12 (mono font).

text_style.description: Explicit overrides on top of the role preset. Omit fields you do not need; a font_size below the role floor is rejected. On update_shape only the stated fields change: alignment, margins, wrap and autosize are kept, so recolouring a badge never un-centres it.

font_name.description: Font name or a design_system font token: heading, body, mono; a token needs design_system.fonts to declare it.

color.description: 6-digit hex color (with or without #) or a design_system color token such as "accent".

shape_id.description: Required for update_shape, update_table and delete_shape.

connector_type.description: add_connector only; default Straight. With semantic anchors, Elbow is rendered as a deterministic orthogonal route instead of host auto-routing. Explicit waypoint routes must use Straight because every route leg is a straight native segment.

end_arrow.description: add_connector only: add one native OOXML triangle line-ending at the final route endpoint. Intermediate route segments never receive arrowheads.

start_anchor.description: Required for node-to-node add_connector operations. Identify the source by shape_name when it is created in this patch, or shape_id when it already exists on the slide. Must be paired with end_anchor and cannot be mixed with raw geometry.

shape_name.description: Stable name of a geometry-owning shape created anywhere in this same slide patch.

shape_id.description: Existing live shape id from list_slide_shapes or a previous presentation_apply_patch result.

offset.description: Position along the edge, default 0.5. The safe range avoids transparent rounded corners; keep 0.5 for non-rectangular shapes.

end_anchor.description: Required for node-to-node add_connector operations. Identify the destination by shape_name when it is created in this patch, or shape_id when it already exists on the slide. Must be paired with start_anchor and cannot be mixed with raw geometry.

shape_name.description: Stable name of a geometry-owning shape created anywhere in this same slide patch.

shape_id.description: Existing live shape id from list_slide_shapes or a previous presentation_apply_patch result.

offset.description: Position along the edge, default 0.5. The safe range avoids transparent rounded corners; keep 0.5 for non-rectangular shapes.

waypoints.description: Optional intermediate route points for one logical connector. Requires start_anchor/end_anchor and connector_type Straight. The executor creates contiguous straight segments and puts end_arrow only on the final segment.

values.description: add_table only: rows of cell strings; the first row is the header when header_row is true (default).

header_fill.description: add_table only: header fill colour (hex or design_system token). Omit for the default unfilled bold header.

header_color.description: add_table only: header text colour (hex or token).

font_size.description: add_table only: cell font size, default 14.

color.description: 6-digit hex color (with or without #) or a design_system color token such as "accent".

z_order.description: update_shape only: move the shape in the slide's stacking order.

color.description: 6-digit hex color (with or without #) or a color token declared in design_system.colors of this or an earlier patch; undeclared tokens are rejected.
6-digit hex color (with or without #) or a design_system color token such as "accent".

left.description: Points from the slide's left edge.

top.description: Points from the slide's top edge.

width.description: Points. At least 0.1 for shapes. In raw add_connector geometry, 0 makes a vertical line and a negative value points left. Omit when using semantic anchors.

height.description: Points. At least 0.1 for shapes. In raw add_connector geometry, 0 makes a horizontal line and a negative value points up. Omit when using semantic anchors.

table_style.description: add_table only. minimal (default): no fills, thin rules between rows, no column borders. host_default: keep PowerPoint's built-in table style.

rule_color.description: add_table only: colour of the rules between rows (hex or token); default the design_system line token, else light grey.

rule_weight.description: add_table only: rule weight in points, default 1.

first_column_bold.description: add_table only: bold row labels in the first column, default true.

highlight_rows.description: add_table only: 1-based table rows (the header is row 1) that carry the message; they get a light tint of highlight_fill.

highlight_columns.description: add_table only: 1-based columns that carry the message; tinted like highlight_rows.

highlight_fill.description: add_table only: tint colour for highlighted rows or columns, default the accent token (a 15% tint of it over white).

column_widths.description: add_table / update_table: one width in points per column.

row_height.description: add_table / update_table: height in points for every row; text that needs more space still grows the row.

cell_styles.description: update_table only: style changes for 1-based cell ranges. Text stays unchanged; change cell text with edit_slide_xml.

fill.description: Hex, token, or "none" to remove the fill.

row_rules.description: update_table only: replace the table's borders with thin rules between rows and no column borders.

assets.description: Image descriptors returned by publish_office_asset, each with a short key referenced by add_image.asset_key.

name: edit_built_chart
description: Replace an existing chart's content with a new spec, keeping the same chart object on the slide (its position, relationship, and shape id). Use this to change a chart's data, form, or styling without touching raw XML: call read_chart_style first, then pass a full replacement spec carrying the returned style and construction. Refuses when the existing chart has a form the builder cannot reproduce (combo, 3D, secondary axis, pie); use edit_slide_chart on the raw XML for those.

slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or verify_slides output.

spec.description: Declarative chart spec: pick the chart form, supply raw numbers and display formats, and the builder emits known-good chart XML following the house construction standard. No OOXML knowledge needed. Fields under properties apply to every form that lists them.

position.description: Chart frame placement in EMU; omit for the full-slide default

style.description: Colors and font the chart uses. Pass the deck's own accent and fonts so charts follow the deck; omitted values fall back to the house palette (blue accent, grays, Calibri), which is only right on the stock theme

accent.description: The one emphasis color; the deck's accent (theme_palette.accent1, or the accent set in the master)

negative.description: Waterfall decreases; defaults to a warm orange

neutral.description: Non-accent bars and lines; defaults to a mid gray

totals.description: Waterfall totals and totals labels; defaults to dark gray

text.description: Label and axis text; defaults to near-black

text_secondary.description: Axis titles, subtitles; defaults to dark gray

bg.description: The slide background behind the chart. Growth-arrow labels and forecast hatching fill against this, so pass it on any deck whose background is not white

ramp.description: Dark-to-light neutral ramp for Likert and stacked segments

font.description: Typeface for every text in the chart; the deck's body font

construction.description: How the chart is constructed. Omit for the house standard. Under a deck standard, read one of the deck's existing charts and set these to match it (legend position, value axis shown or hidden, gridlines); a title inside the chart is the top-level `title`

value_axis.description: House default hidden on bar forms; line and scatter keep theirs

gridlines.description: Horizontal value gridlines; house default off

point_labels.description: Custom label text for specific points, e.g. [{index: 0, text: '16.3 万辆'}]. index is against categories/values in the caller's display order (same convention as categories), regardless of the builder's internal bottom-up storage order for a horizontal bar chart. name: duplicate_slide
description: Duplicate a slide in the presentation. The copy is inserted immediately after the original slide. Returns the new slide_id and source_slide_id. This copies the existing slide and its native content; use presentation_apply_patch to design a new slide.

slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or verify_slides output.

name: import_slides
description: Insert slides from a .pptx the user supplied (a template, a colleague's pages, a reference deck) into this presentation as native slides. The chosen slides keep their source order and land after after_slide_id (default: after the last slide). Returns each source position with its new slide_id; fill or delete their placeholders and verify them like any new slide. Use duplicate_slide to copy a slide of this deck. With keep_source_formatting the deck's original theme stays primary until you move slides onto the imported master or rebuild the theme with edit_slide_master.

asset.description: The .pptx descriptor returned by publish_office_asset (purpose input_pptx), passed unchanged.

source_positions.description: 1-based positions of the slides to import from the source deck. Omit to import every slide.

after_slide_id.description: Current slide id from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata; the imported slides are inserted after it. Omit to append at the end.

formatting.description: use_destination_theme (default) adopts this deck's master; keep_source_formatting keeps the source look and adds its master.

name: copy_image_between_slides
